title: Mutual concessions on reprobation before the controversy on Christ's death
pass_a_gloss: For the rest, things conceded on both sides are these. (1) Nothing happens in time that does not come from God's ordination, and that eternal. (2) Of comparative predestination — of these rather than those — the cause is God's highest good pleasure. (3) The foresight of the reprobate is infallible, whence at least an infallible necessity of the event. (4) Regard to sins, unbelief, and final impenitence enters the decree of reprobation; and no one is damned except for sins as the cause of his own ruin, from the State of the Controversy. (5) God is in no way the cause of sins — neither physical nor moral — nor is any force from the decree brought to bear on those who sin, nor is there in the reprobate any necessity of sinning that destroys the voluntary, the free, and the deliberative, as we have treated at length above. (6) No one can be conscious to himself of reprobation, unless perhaps one sinning against the Holy Spirit. Hence there is always room for repentance, and so for remission of sins and for salvation; God by singular mercy having often worked conversion in the most lost, even in the last struggle, in the final hour, in the very jaws of hell, when every hope of pardon is at last snatched away only after death, and so on. (7) To the reprobate God grants manifold grace — for example of divine forbearance, of kindness, and of outward invitation, from what has been said, and even of inward light.
pass_b_english: Besides this, both sides concede the following.
1. Nothing takes place in time except from God's ordination, and that eternal.
2. In comparative predestination — these rather than those — the cause is God's highest good pleasure.
3. Foresight of the reprobate is infallible, and from it comes at least an infallible necessity of the event.
4. Regard to sins, unbelief, and final impenitence enters the reprobation decree; and no one is damned except for sins as the cause of his own ruin — so the State of the Controversy.

5. God is in no way the cause of sins, neither physical nor moral; no force from the decree is applied to sinners; and in the reprobate there is no necessity of sinning that destroys what is voluntary, free, and of deliberate choice — as we have argued at length above.

6. No one can know himself reprobate, unless perhaps by sinning against the Holy Spirit. So there is always room for repentance, for forgiveness of sins, and for salvation; and God by singular mercy has often worked conversion in the most lost — even in the last agony, in the final hour, in hell's very jaws — when every hope of pardon is finally cut off only after death.
7. God grants the reprobate many kinds of grace: divine forbearance, kindness, and outward invitation, from what we have said, and even inward light.
source_text: Cæterùm concessa utrimque sunt, 1. Nihil fieri in tempore, quod non ex ordinatione Dei, eâque aeterna. 2. Praedestinationis comparatae, horum potius quam illorum, causam esse Dei summum beneplacitum. 3. Praescientiam reproborum esse infallibilem unde saltem necessitas infallibilis eventûs. 4. Intuitum peccatorum, incredulitatis, impaenit. finalis, ingredi decretum Reprobat. nec damnari quemquam nisi propter peccata, ut causam suae perditionis, ex Statu Controv. 5. Deum peccatorum nullo modo causam esse, nec physicam, nec moralem, nec vim ullam ex decreto peccantibus admoveri, neque ullam in reprobis peccandi esse necessitatem destructivam τῷ ἑκουσίῳ, τῷ ἐλευθέρῳ, τῷ προαιρετικῷ, ut nos fusè in superioribus. 6. Reprobationis neminem posse sibi esse conscium, nisi fortè peccantem in Spiritum S. Hinc semper locum esse ut paenitentiae, sic remissioni peccatorum, saluti; Deo singulari misericordiâ operato saepè conversionem in maximè perditis, etiam in extremo agone, horâ ultimâ, in ipsis Orci faucibus, spe omni veniae demum post mortem praereptâ, &c. 7. Reprobis a Deo concedi multiplicem gratiam, puta tolerantiae divinae, beneficentiae, & externae invitationis, ex dictis, etiam interni luminis.
notes: Controv. print pp. 52-53 / PDF ~152-153. Margin: Concessa utrimque. Natural close of Controv. VI before VII. De Morte Christi universali.
